## Review

::: {.question}
Why is the test MSE curve U-shaped?
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.takeaway}
Something improves as flexibility rises, and something degrades.
:::
:::

## Bias-variance decomposition

::: {.vcenter}
$$E\left(y_0 - \hat{f}(x_0)\right)^2 = \text{Var}\left(\hat{f}(x_0)\right) + \left[\text{Bias}\left(\hat{f}(x_0)\right)\right]^2 + \text{Var}(\varepsilon)$$
:::

## Bias and variance {.small}

::: {.definition}
Imagine drawing a new training set from the same population, refitting, and
predicting at the same $x_0$. Repeat many times.
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.incremental}
* **Variance**: how much $\hat{f}(x_0)$ moves across those training sets  
* **Bias**: how far the average $\hat{f}(x_0)$ sits from $f(x_0)$  
:::
:::

## The trade-off

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
### More flexible

Bias $\downarrow$

Variance $\uparrow$
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Less flexible

Bias $\uparrow$

Variance $\downarrow$
:::

::::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.takeaway}
The U is one curve falling plus another rising.
:::
:::

## Bias and variance by data set

![](img/islp/fig2_12.png){fig-align="center" width="90%"}

::: {.source}
ISLP Figure 2.12. Squared bias in blue, variance in orange, $\text{Var}(\varepsilon)$
dashed, and test MSE in red, for the data of Figures 2.9 to 2.11.
:::

## Irreducible error

::: {.takeaway}
Bias and variance can both be driven toward zero with the right model and enough
data. $\text{Var}(\varepsilon)$ cannot.
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.question}
Test MSE is 4.0 and will not go lower. Bad model, or hard problem?
:::
:::

## Classification error rate

::: {.vcenter}
$$\text{Error rate} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} I\left(y_i \neq \hat{y}_i\right)$$
:::
